newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Govt grants petroleum permits off West Australia.
newsitem.headline: Govt grants petroleum permits off West Australia.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday awarded eight new petroleum exploration permits for activity off the coast of the state of Western Australia.

The Australian and state governments said successful companies included Woodside Petroleum Ltd, Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, Mobil Exploration and Producing Australia Pty Ltd, West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd and Gulliver Productions Pty Ltd.

Two areas lie off the Kimberley coast north of Koolan Island, four are north-west of Barrow Island, one west of North West Cape and one west of Rottnest Islands, Australian Resources Minister Warwick Parer and state Mines Minister Norman Moore said.
"During the next six years, an estimated A$540 million will be spent on exploration in these areas," Parer said.
"This includes 78 exploration wells and a significant amount of marine seismic surveying, all playing an important role in Australia's economic future."
"Seven of the eight areas are in the general vicinity of oil and gas discoveries made in recent years, highlighting the potential of the new permits," Parer said.
-- a Shell-led consortium for areas W96-4 and W96-5;
-- a consortium led by Mobil for W96-11;
-- Woodside-headed consortiums for w96-13 and W96-21;
